meta.title: McDonald's Real Business Isn't Burgers. It's Rent.
meta.hook: McDonald's collected more than ten billion dollars in rent from franchised restaurants in twenty twenty-four.
meta.description: McDonald's Corporation owns or controls much of the land and buildings under its restaurants and collects rent from franchisees. Finance chief Harry Sonneborn engineered this structure in the 1950s through McDonald's Franchise Realty Corporation. The burgers pay the bills; the real estate is the business.

scenes.narration: McDonald's collected more than ten billion dollars in rent from franchised restaurants in twenty twenty-four.

visual.visual_intent: A McDonald's storefront and golden arches sign at dusk, low angle, cinematic
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the familiar object, hard cut

scenes.narration: That happens because franchisees do not just pay royalties for the logo and operating system.

visual.query: 1950s businessman office archival black and white
visual.visual_intent: A mid-century office interior, archival documentary feel, a man reviewing papers at a desk, film grain
visual.decision_reason: introduces the financial architect, reported history

scenes.narration: McDonald's generally owns the restaurant land or building, or secures the long-term lease, then charges the franchisee rent.

visual.query: empty commercial lot for lease sign
visual.visual_intent: A vacant corner lot with a 'for lease' sign, wide establishing shot, golden hour
visual.decision_reason: structural fact: McDonald's Franchise Realty Corp, 1956

scenes.narration: Its annual filing says conventional franchisees pay rent and royalties tied to sales, with minimum rent requirements.

visual.query: businessman speaking pointing hand gesture office
visual.visual_intent: A man in a suit gesturing firmly mid-sentence across a desk, high contrast, documentary style
visual.decision_reason: widely reported paraphrase of Sonneborn, marked as reported quote

scenes.narration: At the end of a typical franchise term, McDonald's still controls the underlying real estate and can re-franchise the location.

visual.query: hamburger on tray fast food close up
visual.visual_intent: A simple fast-food hamburger on a tray under warm light, shallow focus, still
visual.decision_reason: the curiosity-gap turn on the product itself

scenes.narration: So every successful restaurant can produce food sales, royalties, and rent while the operator handles the kitchen.

visual.query: aerial view suburban strip mall real estate
visual.visual_intent: An aerial tracking shot over a suburban commercial strip with multiple retail pads, cinematic drone feel
visual.decision_reason: structural fact about McDonald's Corp's land/property holdings model

scenes.narration: The burger brings customers in. Control of the site makes the cash flow unusually durable.

visual.visual_intent: A busy fast-food kitchen with staff working the line, warm light, documentary realism, pulling back
